reviews.title: Update is terrible!
reviews.text: I’ve walked 17,000 miles over 7 years averaging 16:30 minute mile with map my walk. After the latest update it says i now walk 7 miles in 14:39.  That is not feasible for a 71 year old male. Also the home screen has changed by adding steps and pushing average to second page and not allowing me to change or remove the steps which is always at zero.

reviews.title: After update, voice not working
reviews.text: After I updated the app, it started updating my mileage by the 2/3 mile point, which is wrong. Should be announcing it at the mile point. Additionally, the voice response turned off (and I cannot get it to come back on) when all settings indicate it IS on, not only in the app, but in my phone settings. Very disappointed after using this app successfully for many years. 😭💔

reviews.title: Way off!
reviews.text:
Most days I walk 5 1/2 miles with a 1500 foot elevation gain. 

Yet the total distance I walked shows anywhere between 3.8 and 5.5 miles on this app.  
I’ve used this app for years simply because I’m too cheap to pay for anything better, and it does provide a little information…. in my jacket pocket the device reads 3.8 miles. In my pants pocket it reads 5.5 miles… for the exact same route! As a result, the miles per hour and other information is all way off too.

If you’re at all serious about collecting accurate information, find something else. This is fine if you’re just having fun, and the numbers don’t matter. It’s really just another advertising vehicle with bogus challenges from sports companies trying to sell you something.

reviews.title: Completely innacurate
reviews.text:
I have been using this app as a part of my fitness journey for the last couple of years. I have often noticed that when I am hiking and need to take a moment to rest, my calorie burn keeps going up even if I am sitting still. I originally assumed maybe this was just to account for the fact that my heart rate was still up and I possibly could be burning more calories from that. I also wondered if the app was really keeping track of the difference in calories burned from going at an extremely fast pace versus a slow pace and whether it accounted for elevation changes, like hiking up a steep incline versus walking on a flat easy surface. Everything I read online said that the app factored those things in. But I was suspicious, so I put it to an extreme test as follows:

1. I sat in one spot for 10 minutes and let this app “track“ my hike. It actually showed considerable calories burned, as if I were actually exercising. I tracked this and noted the calorie burn.
2. I then started over, got in my car and drove 60 mph on a highway uphill in a mountainous area. The calorie burn was exactly identical to when I was doing nothing!

Conclusion: there is no possible way the app is keeping track of your actual speed and elevation change when it calculates calories.
